correctness.rationale: For \(0<c\le1\), the exponential central mass is exactly \(2e^{-1}\sinh c\); for \(c\ge1\), it is \(1-e^{-1-c}\). In the first regime the derivative sign is controlled by \(R_-(c)=e^{-1}\cosh(c)/\phi(c)\), whose logarithmic derivative is \(c+\tanh c>0\). In the second regime the derivative sign is controlled by \(R_+(c)=e^{-1-c}/(2\phi(c))\), whose logarithmic derivative is \(c-1>0\). Mills bounds give \(D(1)>0\) and show the large-radius difference approaches zero from below. These facts prove exactly one positive zero in each regime and the full sign pattern. The bundled checker only reproduces numerical root brackets.
